audit.whatIsWrong: Labelled EVEN at 6/10 while the win rate is 45.17% over 518 games and the chart already gives Jax 4 of 7 stages with Trundle winning none.
audit.why: 518 games is the third-largest sample in the slice and 45.17% is not an even lane. Every prose field in the entry describes losing — 'your trades outside W are losing', 'the duel-flipper that makes this matchup survivable at all'.
audit.corrected: diff to HARD, tone to the hard colour, and 6/10 to 7/10 in diffRating, breakdown.difficulty and the final rating line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is named as the matchup-defining cooldown eleven times across the entry and never once given a duration, so 'bait it then commit' has no window attached.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s. The bait window nearly halves as she ranks it, which is precisely why the lane gets worse from level 2 to level 9 — that trend is the useful fact and it needs the numbers to exist. Leap Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s and Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110/100/90s.
audit.corrected: Added 17s at rank 1 falling to 9s at rank 5, and the 110s R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grandmaster-at-Arms is described twice as a passive that showers Jax with 'massive bonus armor and MR every third auto'. It does not. The third-attack component is bonus magic damage; the Armor and MR come from activating R.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Every third consecutive attack deals additional Magic Damage. Additionally, Jax can activate this ability to deal damage around himself and strengthen his resolve, increasing his Armor and Magic Resist for a short duration.' This matters enormously to a Trundle: a visible 110-second button you can wait out is a completely different problem from resists that accrue silently while you fight.
audit.corrected: Split the two halves of R and named the activation as the resist source.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is again credited with an attack-speed steal ('the Chomp AS-steal proc', 'dodge the attack-speed debuff'). It saps Attack Damage only. Relatedly, the entry says Counter Strike lets Jax 'negate your Chomp auto', which reads as though your bite is dodged too.
audit.why: Riot text: Counter Strike — 'Jax's combat prowess allows him to dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration.' Attacks, not abilities. Chomp is a cast, so it goes through the dodge window and only your basic attacks are wasted. That single distinction changes what you hold and what you spend inside his E.
audit.corrected: Removed the attack-speed claim and stated that Chomp lands through Counter Strike while your autos do not.

audit.whatIsWrong: Empower is never mentioned, so the reader has no burst tell.
audit.why: Empower is a 7/6/5/4/3s auto-attack reset that loads his next attack. The weapon glow, not the Leap Strike, is the cue that the damage is coming.
audit.corrected: Named Empower (W) as the tell in whys[1].

edits.before: Level 1 is the one window you can reasonably contest — Chomp steals his AD on the first trade and denies him the flat-damage edge Jax normally exploits early. Take the exchange and back off before he can chain autos. The moment he hits level 2 and has Counter Strike, the calculus shifts: he can jump on you, pop E to dodge your next auto and the Chomp AS-steal proc, and stun you while you are standing still inside what is supposed to be your Frozen Domain power island. At level 3 his kit is fully online and yours is too, but his Counter Strike makes your W zone a liability — he can brawl inside it willingly because the stun interrupts your healing window. Farm safely, stay at 50-60% HP so a stun combo plus Leap Strike burst does not one-shot you, and do not waste Pillar on a minion push.
edits.after: Level 1 is the one window you can reasonably contest — Chomp saps his AD on the first trade and denies him the flat-damage edge Jax normally exploits early. Take the exchange and back off before he chains autos. The moment he hits level 2 and has Counter Strike, the calculus shifts: he jumps on you, pops E, and stuns you while you stand inside what is supposed to be your Frozen Domain power island. Counter Strike dodges attacks, not abilities, so hold your autos through it and keep Chomping. At level 3 both kits are online but his E still makes your W zone a liability, because the stun lands mid-heal. Farm safely, stay above 60% HP so a stun into Leap Strike cannot one-shot you, and never waste Pillar on a minion push.

edits.before: Jax hits level 2 and Counter Strike turns every W-zone trade into his window — he dodges your autos, stacks the dodge bonus, then stuns you mid-heal.
edits.after: Jax hits level 2 and Counter Strike turns every W-zone trade into his window — he eats your autos, then stuns you mid-heal. Watch the Empower glow, not the jump.

edits.before: With Q+W+E Jax can Leap Strike onto you, pop Counter Strike to negate your Chomp auto, and stun you while Frozen Domain is still underneath you — the zone does not protect you from a stun reset.
edits.after: With Q+W+E Jax can Leap Strike onto you, pop Counter Strike to eat your basic attacks, and stun you while Frozen Domain is still underneath — the zone does not save you from the stun.

edits.before: Late game you are still a relevant duelist if Subjugate is up, but Jax's R passive granting him massive bonus armor and MR every third auto means the longer a fight drags, the more he catches up on the resist race you opened. Play side lane confidently — few champions 1v1 you inside Frozen Domain with Subjugate available — but do not take 50/50 duels with R on cooldown. In team fights your role is to ulti their beefiest frontliner and peel through them; fighting Jax directly in a 5v5 is not your priority when your drain ultimate can steal a Malphite or Ornn's entire stat budget. If Jax is already fed coming into this phase, respect it: farm, contest objectives with your team, and save Subjugate for a pick rather than a suicide duel.
edits.after: Late game you are still a relevant duelist if Subjugate is up, but Grandmaster-at-Arms is an activation, not a third-auto trickle: when Jax presses R on its 110-second cooldown he takes on Armor and MR outright and claws back the resist race you opened. The third-attack half of R is only bonus magic damage. Play side lane confidently — few champions 1v1 you inside Frozen Domain with Subjugate available — but never take 50/50 duels with R down. In team fights, ulti their beefiest frontliner and peel; fighting Jax directly in a 5v5 is not your priority when your drain ultimate can take a Malphite or Ornn's entire stat budget. If Jax is already fed coming into this phase, respect it: farm, contest objectives, and save Subjugate for a pick.

edits.before: Two items on Jax means his R passive showers him with extra resists every few autos, partially undoing your Subjugate lead — duel him only when R is available, split-push when it is not.
edits.after: Two items on Jax means pressing Grandmaster-at-Arms hands him a block of Armor and MR that partly undoes your Subjugate lead — duel only when your own R is up, split-push when it is not.

edits.before: Late-game Jax's R passive makes him effectively tankier than his item sheet suggests, so your Subjugate gains value — but he usually has enough of a lead to make you chase rather than duel.
edits.after: Late-game Jax activates Grandmaster-at-Arms for Armor and MR on demand, so your Subjugate gains value — but he usually has enough of a lead by then to make you chase rather than duel.

notes: Disk 45.17% / 518; packet says 45.75% / 400 — close enough that the difficulty correction is safe either way. Confidence on the Counter-Strike-does-not-dodge-Chomp point is Medium rather than High: Riot's wording is 'dodge all incoming attacks', which excludes ability casts, and Chomp is a cast rather than a basic attack — but the kit file's needsResearch block is empty, so this is read off the tooltip rather than confirmed, and it is worth one verification pass before it goes live.
